correctness.rationale: At critical density the Zak transform is unitary with dx/a dtheta/(2pi), giving exact essential extrema as sharp constants. For each Laplace component, the real-part gap equals r(1-r)(1+cos(theta))/[(1+r)(1+r^2-2r cos(theta))]>=0; integrable mixing preserves the inequality; x approaching a and theta=pi saturate it, while x approaching 0 and theta=0 saturate the triangle upper bound. Fejer means contradict any Bessel bound for 1/2<p<=1; the remaining p range and special constants follow by gamma integral and zeta identities. A finite numerical checker is supplemental only.

value.rationale: Sharp lower and upper constants for an infinite-dimensional family of positive Laplace mixtures are natural exact spectral invariants; boundary saturation is a structural lemma, not a numeric sample. For power tails the result supplies a complete L2 Bessel/frame classification and exact zeta/eta condition number with a quantified divergence at p=1. The p=2 exact lower bound improves a valid but nonsharp coarse constant of 1/64 to (1-pi^2/12)^2.
